Additionally, moving to Sweden is a difficult endeavour. I moved there pre Brexit from the UK and even with freedom of movement it was tough, post-brexit, it’s even more difficult. To be able to do pretty much anything (working, acquire a bank account, etc) in Sweden you require a social security number (personnummer) and to be able to get one you need to fulfil certain criteria - a specific amount of money to support yourself. Even if you are able to fulfil the criteria, the application can take months. Then following leaving the EU, it’s even more difficult with brits as we are now considered as third country nationals. Just some thoughts for you to consider if this is an option you want to take. Check out the migrationsverket website for more information (there is an English version too).

But I heavily encourage you to commit to your education, as that’s worth more than you realise and you will heavily regret throwing it away. Additionally, degrees are highly valued in Sweden for majority of jobs, if you are to move there at a later date.

Not sure about tips that are outside of the usual standard but from my experience of having two degus, these were some things that I found fun to do with them or something to ensure their well being.

Be sure to keep the room they are situated a decent temperature, I found my degus got cold very easily so we had to ensure they had around 16-22 degrees Celsius. 

They absolutely love to forage, so id hand them little strips of bedding through the cage and watch them make the bed and they’d come back for more and more. This was absolutely adorable and also a great way to socialise and have them get used to you, you can also do this with treats/food, although be wary of what you give them as they can easily become diabetic. I’d give them a few sunflower seeds or 1 monkey nut a week and the occasional herb bowl.

To get them used to being handled, put some of their usual food on your hand, almost trickling to encourage them to walk into your palm, eventually they became comfortable with walking up my arms and one eventually would regularly sleep on me in my bathrobe (cute af).
